So, the life cycle analysis of the project is estimated based on annual CO capture capacity 2 only. 9.1 Methodology and Approach The cost estimation for this project has been done according to NETL (National Energy Technology Laboratory) guidelines defined in “Quality Guidelines for Energy System Studies (QGESS)” published by NETL and AACE 16R-90 (Conducting Technical and Economic Evaluations – As Applied for the Process and Utility Industries). Cost estimation for this project is consistent with the requirement and consideration for the Association for the Advancement of Cost Engineering (AACE) Class 4. The scope of this estimation includes the capital cost of major units like the CCU unit, the WGS unit, compressors, etc., and the capital cost of balance of plant facilities like utility systems, CHP, LP boilers, water systems, electrical systems, instrumentation, etc. Capital cost is defined at five levels: Bare Erected Cost (BEC), Engineering, Procurement, and Construction Cost (EPCC), Total Plant Cost (TPC), Total Overnight Cost (TOC), and Total As-Spent Cost (TASC). BEC, EPCC, TPC, and TOC are expressed based on ‘base-year’ dollars, where the base year is the first year of capital expenditure. On the other hand, TASC is expressed in mixed, current-year dollars over the whole capital expenditure period, including their escalation. A schematic of the same has been presented in Figure 5. • BEC consists of the cost of process instruments, onsite auxiliary facilities, ancillary facilities, and direct and indirect labor for construction and erection. • EPCC consists of BEC and the cost of EPC services. The EPC services include detailed design, contractor permitting, and project/construction management costs. • TPC comprises EPCC, project, and process contingencies. Process contingency is considered to compensate for the cost due to process uncertainties regarding efficiency, run rate, and campaign life. At the same time, project contingency is deemed to compensate lack of project definition. • TOC includes TPC, overnight costs consisting of owner’s costs (excluding escalation during construction and interest during construction). The owner cost consisting prepaid royalties, pre- production cost, inventory capital, land, financing cost, and other owner’s cost. Preproduction cost Attachment-7: Initial Engineering Design and Cost Estimate 23 DE-FE0031937 / 0009 includes start-up expenses for the plant's commercial operation after the project's completion. Inventory capital allocation is made for initial inventory build-up during commercial operation. Financing costs include securing financing for the project (upfront fees, financial closing costs, etc.). And other owner’s cost covers the cost of feasibility studies, legal fees, permitting cost, owner’s engineering, management reserve, and external infrastructure. • TASC is the sum of all capital expenditures, including escalation and interest during construction (IDC).
